p0.original: 第十二章 心理障碍

p1.en: Translator of this chapter: Chen Kung-hyang

p3.original: 本章视频导读，请扫描二维码观看。
p3.en: Scan the QR code to watch the video introduction to this chapter.

p4.original: 在阅读本章之前，请你思考一个问题：身为神志正常者，你愿意伪装成病人住进精神病院吗？也许你会说：“什么？”“太疯狂了！”“我不愿意！”但是，在1973年，美国斯坦福大学的研究人员大卫·罗森汉（David Rosenhan）就曾招募了8名健康的志愿者，把他们“送”进了精神病院，结果，其中7人被诊断为“精神分裂症”。看到这，很多人都会大吃一惊：“为什么会这样？”是因为“精神病院的环境”还是因为“精神健康从业人员不够专业”？我们又该“如何优化心理障碍的诊断流程”？如果你想知道答案，就请继续读下去，本章将从罗森汉的实验出发，为你讲解“心理障碍”的那些事儿。
p4.en: Before reading this chapter, please think about the question: Are you willing to live in a mental institution as a patient, as a person with a normal mind? Maybe you'd say, "What? "It's crazy! "I don't want to! However, in 1973, David Rosenhan, a researcher at Stanford University in the United States, recruited eight healthy volunteers and placed them in psychiatric institutions, which resulted in the diagnosis of “schizophrenia” in seven of them. Seeing this, a lot of people would be surprised: "Why is that? Is it because of “the mental health institution environment” or because “mental health practitioners are not professional enough”? And how can we “optimise the process of diagnosis of mental disorders”? If you want to know the answer, continue reading, and this chapter will start with Rosenham's experiment to explain the “psychological handicap” to you.

p5.original: 那么，什么是心理障碍？对于该问题我们走过了很长的一段探索路程，医学模型和心理模型对它的看法是不一样的，但是目前有融合的趋势。现代生物心理学认为，许多精神障碍不仅涉及认知、行为、发展和社会文化因素，还涉及大脑和神经系统。
p5.en: So, what's the mental disorder? We have come a long way in exploring this issue, and medical and psychological models differ in their perception of it, but there is a trend towards integration. Modern biopsychology believes that many mental disorders relate not only to cognitive, behavioural, developmental and sociocultural factors, but also to the brain and nervous system.

p6.original: 心理障碍不是仅存在于书本之上，更多的是发生在你我身边。你是否有朋友长期情绪低落，甚至患有抑郁症？你是否因为考试而担心、焦虑。你的孩子是否过度活跃、注意力不集中？这些问题在DSM-5中都会给出科学的、明确的界定。此外，本章集中讨论了我们在日常生活中最有可能遇到的各类精神障碍，如抑郁症、双相障碍、焦虑症、强迫症、精神分裂症以及各类神经发育障碍等。在这里你将了解到不同精神障碍的分类、诊断标准、发病率和可能的致病因素。阅读完本章后你将极大地增进对心理障碍的认识，不同类型障碍既有区别又有联系，值得你细细探究。
p6.en: The mental disorder is not just on the books, it's more happening to you and me. Do you have any friends who are chronically depressed or even depressed? Are you worried about your exams? Is your child overactive and insensitive? These issues are defined scientifically and clearly in DSM-5. In addition, this chapter focuses on the types of mental disorders that we are most likely to encounter in our daily lives, such as depression, bipolar disorders, anxiety, stress disorder, schizophrenia and various types of neurodevelopmental disorders. Here you will learn about the classification of different mental disorders, diagnostic criteria, morbidity and possible causes of illness. After reading this chapter, you will greatly improve your understanding of the psychological barriers, which are different and related and deserve your detailed attention.

p7.original: 当然，DSM-5并非万能，它根据症状而不是病因来对各类障碍进行分类，这让许多临床医生对DSM-5分类系统持有保留意见，并希望有更好的分类系统来取代它，因为研究发现许多看似不同的疾病都涉及相同基因的异常——这表明它们可能在大脑中有共同的生物学基础。而根据症状对精神障碍进行分类忽略了大脑中的实际情况，不利于我们找到病因并进行有效的治疗。近年来，神经成像技术、经颅磁刺激、经颅磁直流电刺激在心理障碍的研究中应用较多，相信借助这些先进的技术，未来我国对心理障碍的发病机制和治疗方案的研究会迈上一个新台阶。
p7.en: Of course, DSM-5 is not a panacea. It categorizes barriers according to symptoms rather than cause, which leads many clinicians to express reservations about the DSM-5 classification system and wants to have a better classification system to replace it, because research has found that many diseases seemingly different are related to the same genetic anomalies — suggesting that they may have a common biological basis in the brain. The classification of mental disorders by symptoms ignores the reality in the brain and prevents us from finding the cause of the disease and treating it effectively. In recent years, neuroimaging techniques, brain magnetic irritation, and brain-magnetic direct-flow electric irritation have been used more in the study of mental disorders, and it is believed that, with these advanced technologies, future research on the mechanisms for the development of mental disorders and treatment programmes in our country will take a new step forward.

p8.original: 总而言之，心理障碍是一个非常宏大的领域，受到心理学、医学、精神病学等多个学科的专家和研究人员的关注。请记住，阅读本章并不能使你成为心理障碍方面的专家，请不要随便为别人做诊断、贴标签。人们对心理障碍病因的探索一直在继续。人类的精神世界异彩纷呈，各类障碍无疑是无数精神之花中的一朵。人生百般滋味，生活仍需笑对。
p8.en: In sum, mental disorders are a very ambitious area that is of interest to specialists and researchers in various disciplines, including psychology, medicine and psychiatry. Please remember that reading this chapter does not make you an expert in psychological disorders, and do not just make diagnostics or labels for others. The search for the causes of mental disorders has continued. The spiritual world of humankind is diverse, and obstacles of all kinds are undoubtedly one of countless spiritual flowers. Life is so good that life still has to laugh.

p11.original: 1889年，文森特·梵高（Vincent Van Gogh）因精神问题在阿尔勒医院（Arles Hospital）接受了几个月的治疗。
p11.en: In 1889 Vincent Van Gogh was treated at Arles Hopital for mental problems for several months.
